correctness.rationale: The forward solution separates to \(Kt=B g(F/B)\), where \(g(u)=u-\log(1+u)\). The two-time ratio \(R_\rho(u)=g(\rho u)/g(u)\) is strictly decreasing: its logarithmic elasticity \(h(u)=u^2/[(1+u)g(u)]\) decreases because \(H(u)=u^2/(u+2)-g(u)\) has \(H(0)=0\) and \(H'(u)=u^2/[(1+u)(u+2)^2]>0\). The quotient runs from \(\rho^2\) to \(\rho\), giving strict feasibility and global uniqueness. The upper asymptotic follows the third-order series of \(g\); the lower follows \(R_\rho(u)-\rho\sim(\rho-1)\log(u)/u\) and its inversion. The included code passed exact rational checks and 4,000 reproducible positive-parameter inversions; finite tests are not used as the proof of the universal statement.

originality.rationale: Classical Green–Ampt forward infiltration and hydraulic-parameter inversion are credited as prior work. Relevant full-text portions of the 2005 falling-head inverse study, 2009 resistivity inverse study, and 2015 infiltration/redistribution study were compared by assumptions and logical implication, and none of the inspected claims covered the combined exact two-point constant-ponding feasibility wedge and sharp asymmetric parameter boundary laws. Historical priority remains provisional for Warrick (1993), the unavailable full text of Mohammadzadeh-Habili and Heidarpour (2011), and any broader analytical inverse theorem.
residual_risks: Full original text of Warrick (1993) was not compared; a more general analytical inverse-scaling result could imply part of the classification.
Mohammadzadeh-Habili and Heidarpour (2011) full text was inaccessible; its abstract alone does not decide novelty.
A broad global inverse-function or Bernstein-function elasticity theorem may subsume portions of the proof even if its application to this physical model has not been located.
No independent referee or external validation has been performed.

value.rationale: The exact observation-domain wedge lets a two-measurement infiltration experiment reject this ideal physical model before parameter fitting, and yields global rather than local parameter identifiability whenever feasible. Quantified pole and logarithmic boundary degenerations provide distinct calibration-sloppiness scales that are not contained in standard numerical fit results. The domain and limits are intrinsic to the physical cumulative-infiltration observable, with no arbitrary finite cutoff or synthetic parameter restriction. The finding does not claim real-soil noise robustness.
